quote: our emotions arise from our models of reality
content: Bidirectional causation is an argument for the essay’s thesis, not against it. If a belief was produced by hunger or weather rather than by evidence, that belief is inaccurate, and the emotion resting on it is by the essay’s own criterion irrational — which is the diagnosis the annotation says the criterion cannot make. The evidential base offered for the reverse arrow is also weaker than presented: Schachter and Singer’s misattribution study is among the most famous non-replications in social psychology, with the key emotion-transfer effects failing in direct replications (Marshall & Zimbardo 1979; Maslach 1979). Johnson and Tversky’s mood effect is real and is a bias to be corrected, which is the book’s subject.

quote: That which the truth nourishes should thrive.
content: Depressive realism is one of the weakest findings invoked against the maxim. The meta-analysis reports an overall effect near zero once judgment domain and design are controlled, with the pattern confined to specific contingency-estimation tasks (Moore & Fresco 2012), and the Taylor–Brown thesis that illusion is characteristic of mental health has been challenged on measurement grounds, with the "illusion" indices largely tracking narcissism and defensiveness (Colvin & Block 1994). Even granting the effect, it concerns beliefs about the self, and it establishes at most that one narrow class of false belief has a local benefit. The maxim is a claim about what happens when truth is available, not a claim that no comforting falsehood ever pays.

quote: Since the days of Socrates at least, and probably long before, the way to appear cultured and sophisticated has been to never let anyone see you care strongly about anything.
content: Plato is the counterexample to the counterexample. Republic X banishes the tragic poets precisely because they nourish the emotional part of the soul at reason’s expense, and in the Phaedo Socrates rebukes his weeping friends and sends Xanthippe away so that the death can be conducted with composure. Stoic apatheia, on which the sage is undisturbed by passion, became the dominant elite ideal of the Hellenistic and Roman world. The sentimental traditions listed here are real and later; the essay’s claim is that the pose of unmoved sophistication has been prestigious since Socrates, and Socrates’ own student wrote the founding text of it.

quote: My sadness on waking is rational; there is no truth which destroys it.
content: The essay offers a sufficient condition, not a definition, and the listed cases are not counterexamples to a sufficient condition. Grief for a fictional character is standardly explained without any false belief, by imaginative participation in a represented situation (Walton 1978, "Fearing Fictions," Journal of Philosophy, no DOI), so it is not an emotion resting on an error either. The phobic who knows the spider is harmless is the essay’s own paradigm of an emotion that a truth should destroy and does not, which is why the essay says the test is whether a truth destroys it, not whether one has been told the truth. A criterion that classifies some emotions as rational, some as irrational, and leaves moods unclassified is doing the work it was introduced to do.
